SMALL CAUSES JUDGE, MEMBER, MACT-3, BANGALORE, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT

WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA
ORAL JUDGMENT
In this appeal, apart from seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioner is challenging the dismissal of claim petition against the Insurance Company.
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties will be referred to as per the status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 18.01.2011 the petitioner was traveling in a Maruthi Van bearing Reg.No.KA-04/M-2663, near Canara Bank junction at ISRO Layout, Bengaluru, a Canter Lorry bearing NC: 2024:KHC:37349 Reg.No.KA-12-8373 came from opposite direction and dashed against the Maruthi Van, due to which, he sustained head injuries.
After taking treatment, the petitioner has approached the Tribunal through her guardian-father for grant of compensation.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

The Tribunal, after taking the evidence and hearing both the parties by the impugned judgment and award allowed the claim petition against the owners of the Canter Lorry and Maruthi Van and dismissed the claim petition against the Insurance Company of the Maruthi Van by assessing compensation of Rs.89,900/- with interest at 8% p.a.
Pleading inadequacy, seeking enhancement of compensation and challenging dismissal of the claim petition against the Insurance Company, the petitioner is before this Court on various grounds.
4. Heard the arguments of Shri.Chethan B. and Smt.Mamatha D.N., learned counsels for the petitioner NC: 2024:KHC:37349 and Shri E.I.Sanmathi, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

2

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the Maruthi Van was insured with the Insurance Company, policy of insurance was in force, the Insurance Company is liable to indemnify the insured.
The Tribunal has erroneously dismissed the claim against the Insurance Company.
It is further contended that the petitioner is a specially disabled lady, aged 23 years, sustained head injuries with fracture of skull, she was under hospitalization for 12 days.
No compensation is awarded for loss of income during laid up and future medical expenses and even compensation awarded under different heads is inadequate and sought for enhancement.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the accident was caused by the Canter Lorry, the owner of the canter lorry is alone made as a party, which shows that NC: 2024:KHC:37349 the canter lorry is not covered with valid insurance.
The Maruthi Van was covered with only 'Act Policy' at the time of accident, the petitioner was inmate of the Maruthi Van under the Act policy, her risk is not covered.
The Tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim against the Insurance Company and he has supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed by the learned counsel for parties and perused the records.

8. The materials on record point out that the accident took place between Maruthi Van and the Canter Lorry at ISRO Layout, in which the petitioner has sustained head injuries, she was under hospitalization for 12 days at Sagar Hospital, Banashankari.
The charge sheet was filed against the driver of the canter lorry for his actionable negligence.

The owner of the Canter Lorry is the first respondent, who has to shoulder his responsibility for payment of NC: 2024:KHC:37349 compensation and at the same time, respondent No.2 being the owner of the Maruthi Van equally held liable and the claim is rightly filed against them.

9. Having sustained fracture of skull, since the petitioner is a specially disabled lady, same has to be compensated with Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.56,400/- towards medical expenses,
incidental expenses such as attendant, food and nourishment and conveyance charges together at Rs.15,000/-, loss of amenities and discomfort at Rs.30,000/-, towards loss of income during laid up period at Rs.26,000/- (Rs.6,500/- x 4 months) and Rs.10,000/- towards future medical expenses.
Thus, in all, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,67,400/- as against Rs.89,900/- awarded by the Tribunal, thereby enhancement of Rs.77,500/-.
It is the just compensation which the petitioner is entitled to, in the facts and circumstances of the case.
As regarding liability is concerned, as rightly argued by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that Maruthi Van was covered with only Act Policy.
The petitioner was an inmate, no premium was paid for the inmate of the Maruthi Van.
There is no insurance covering the risk of the petitioner.
Hence, the Tribunal is right in dismissing the claim against the Insurance Company.

3 held liable to pay the compensation.

11. In view of the above discussion, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award is modified.
(iii) The petitioner would be entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.77,500/- with NC: 2024:KHC:37349 interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation.

(iv) Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally held liable to pay the compensation and are directed to deposit entire compensation with interest at 6%
p.a. within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
